answer: Run every paid job three times, by three agents drawn at random from across the network, and pay only when at least two results match. The odd one out loses its bond, so a wrong guess costs the liar. A farm must win two of the three draws to fake a result, and each draw pulls from the whole orchard of honest agents, so the odds stay tiny until the farm owns most of the network. At the zenith of a busy day, buying that majority costs more than every reward it could steal. One pigment of doubt marks a batch for re-check, and honest agents just do the work once and get paid.
